concerns: Assay sensitivity and recovery: Short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue sampling may yield EV concentrations near or below detection limits; negative exposure readouts could reflect assay insensitivity rather than true absence of intact EVs (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Spike-in validity: Exogenous tracer behavior may not faithfully model endogenous EV pharmacokinetics or membrane stability in vivo; differential trafficking or clearance of the spike-in could confound recovery-based inference (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Species and route generalizability: Positive rodent intranasal outcomes do not guarantee intact-EV delivery in larger species or humans; macaque data show strong nasal retention and negligible brain uptake for certain EV preparations, so a rodent-positive result may not predict translational delivery (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome).

Specificity of microglial transcriptional readout: Microglial single-cell signatures can be affected by tissue harvest, anesthesia, or systemic inflammatory signals; predefined, validated modules and appropriate non-EV controls (vehicle, soluble secretome, detergent/protease) are required to avoid misattribution (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Feasibility of capture-depleted and particle-matched arms: Generating particle-count–matched but capture-depleted material without altering other bioactive components is technically challenging; incomplete depletion or co-removal of soluble factors could muddy comparisons (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Timing and kinetics: The optimal short post-dose window for detecting intact-EV exposure and consequent microglial transcriptional changes is uncertain; poorly chosen intervals risk false negatives or capturing secondary, non–EV-mediated effects (ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Interpretation if orthogonal metrics disagree: Scenarios where spike-in recovery is low but a microglial signature is observed (or vice versa) will be difficult to interpret without additional controls (e.g., labeled endogenous-EV tracers, longitudinal sampling) (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Statistical reproducibility and sample size: The proposal's success criterion requires reproducibility across animals and conditioned-medium preps; small n or batch variability could produce misleading conclusions—predefinition of n and independent preps is essential (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
conclusion: The proposed in vivo→ex vivo bridge is conceptually plausible and well-aligned with MISEV2023 recommendations: orthogonal, membrane-protection controls plus an exogenous spike-in and single-cell microglial readout could, in principle, distinguish intact-EV–dependent short-interval PD from soluble-secretome effects in rodents. Prior rodent intranasal reports of functional outcomes (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi) make the mechanistic question relevant, while MISEV2023 (ev-misev2023-quality-framework) explicitly supports the need for orthogonal capture/protection assays and appropriate controls. However, there is high uncertainty in translating intranasal intact-EV exposure across species and formulations (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution), and several technical and interpretive risks must be mitigated before a causal attribution to intact EVs can be claimed. If implemented with the proposed orthogonal controls, detergent/protease arms, and validated spike-in recovery, the experiment is capable of discriminating the key competing explanations (intact-EV–mediated vs secretome-mediated effects), but success depends critically on assay sensitivity, spike-in validity, timing/sample recovery, and predefined microglial module selection.
